tagline: A local, transparent spreadsheet-shaped budgeting ledger
verdictSummary: Tiller's actual product is less an app and more an automated feed into a spreadsheet you already control — that's a genuinely honest, buildable idea: import bank CSV or OFX exports into a real spreadsheet-shaped local ledger with deterministic categorization rules you can inspect. What doesn't survive: live, automatic bank-feed connections (no screen-scraping or aggregator here, on purpose) and the maintained template library Tiller sells.
coreLoopDIY: Import CSV or OFX transaction exports into a local ledger, apply inspectable categorization rules, and export the result into spreadsheet-ready views for budget and net-worth tracking.
whatYouLose: support when a bank feed breaks
whyPeopleStillPay: The spreadsheet-shaped ledger is easy to copy; keeping the bank connections themselves alive as institutions change their export formats without warning is the unglamorous, ongoing part.
prompt: Build a local, spreadsheet-shaped budgeting ledger that imports bank transaction exports rather than connecting live to bank accounts — no screen-scraping or third-party aggregation, by design. Use a Next.js/TypeScript app with SQLite, or, if you'd rather stay closer to Tiller's actual model, a Google Sheets API integration that writes into a spreadsheet template you own — either is a legitimate approach. Support CSV and OFX import with a saved column-mapping per bank (so re-importing the same bank's export doesn't require re-mapping every time), and duplicate-transaction detection by date, amount, and description matching. Implement accounts, categories, payees, and split transactions (one transaction covering multiple categories). Add deterministic categorization rules — if description contains X, categorize as Y — that are visible and editable, not a black-box classifier, so every categorization can be traced back to the rule that produced it. Build budget, cash-flow, and net-worth views computed directly from the ledger. Keep an immutable import log so you can always see exactly what was imported and when. Do not build live bank-account connections, payment initiation, or tax/accounting compliance features — those are explicitly out of scope; this is an import-and-categorize ledger, not a bank aggregator. No API key needed for the CSV/OFX path; the Sheets API path needs a free Google Cloud project credential.

faq.q: Does it connect directly to my bank the way Tiller does?
faq.a: No — on purpose. This build only imports files you download from your bank yourself (CSV or OFX), which avoids the security and reliability risks of screen-scraped bank connections entirely.

faq.q: How much manual work is importing each month?
faq.a: A few minutes — download your bank's export, drop it in, and saved column mappings mean you're not re-configuring the import every time, though it's still a manual step Tiller's live feeds skip.

faq.q: Can I keep using it inside a spreadsheet like Tiller does?
faq.a: Yes, if you build the Google Sheets API variant described in the prompt — it writes into a real spreadsheet you own, matching Tiller's actual product shape rather than being a separate app.

faq.q: Is this safe for tracking real bank data?
faq.a: It's as safe as any local tool handling sensitive data — nothing is transmitted anywhere on its own, but you're responsible for backups and device security, since there's no vendor doing that for you here.
